newsitem.title: USA: Architects show plans for proposed Astros Stadium.
newsitem.headline: Architects show plans for proposed Astros Stadium.

text.p: The Houston Astros said architects unveiled plans Wednesday for a proposed state-of-the-art downtown baseball stadium that would host the team's home opener in the year 2000.
Design highlights include include a retractable roof, a technologically advanced sound system and a fully-irrigated natural grass playing field, an Astros' release said.
Quoted in the release, Houston Mayor Bob Lanier said the design "adds a spark of excitement to downtown at an affordable price."
The Mayor added that stadiums built recently have helped revive downtowns of Baltimore and Denver, and Houston can expect the same results when the proposed stadium is built.
Harris County Judge Robert Eckels said he is excited that the stadium's design is moving forward, but cited pending legislation.

"...We have to keep focused on legislative issues pending in Austin, and we must continue the recent progress to ensure this stadium and the improvements for the Astrodome and Rodeo become reality," Eckels said in the release.
Rob Matwick, the team's director of media relations, said several bills are circulating.
"But none have been passed into law," he said. "Until that happens, obviously then there is no financing vehicle."

According to a report prepared by the Houston Sports Facility Advisory Committee, a new stadium will provide thousands of new jobs, including temporary construction, permanent maintenance, and administrative staff.

The Ballpark at Union Station will be located on approximately 25 acres of land at the east side of downtown Houston, at the corner of Crawford and Texas streets, only a few blocks from the George R. Brown Convention Center.
Groundbreaking for Houston's Ballpark at Union Station is planned for later this year.
